messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated CUDA OOMs on serving-pool-7 (rate spike 00:12). 5% of requests failing with OOM even though node headroom reports ~1.2GB free. Auto-escalating to oncall. :bangbang:

maria: saw the same, spikes started after the 02:10 canary rollout. Noted higher fragmentation metric on allocator (frag_ratio -> 0.62).

akshay: grabbing logs now. any customer-facing errors?

maria: yes — a few 503s from chat endpoints, mainly long-context requests. Short queries mostly fine.

jamie: putting preliminary triage: sounds like reserved block mismatch + KV cache growth. We saw similar when prefix cache held large states and reserved pool didn't reflect soft-reservations.

kevin: posting recent dmesg and runtime stack traces here:
```
E CudaOOM: failed to allocate 134217728 bytes
Allocator: free_headroom=1.2GB reserved_blocks=3 last_evicted_ts=161.
Fragmentation metrics: max_free_block=256MB median_free_block=12MB
KV cache entries: 8.4k (avg value 1.2MB)
```

maria: interesting — max_free_block small relative to single request peak. allocator shows many small free slabs.

akshay: I can repro locally-ish by replaying a long-chat workload with repeated tool-calls. The KV cache grows with repeated prefixes and isn't evicting until mem pressure. Seems reserve accounting assumes contiguous block allocation but kernel is fragmented.

jamie: mitigation options: 1) force daemon to compact/free long-lived KV cache per-model, 2) enable aggressive evict policy (lower threshold), 3) drain affected nodes and shift traffic to dedicated spare pool (slow), 4) rollback canary to previous model variant (fast but disruptive).

kevin: ops-bot: initiate node drain on serving-pool-7?
ops-bot: acknowledged. starting drain for node-7a, node-7b; moving active sessions off node-7a (live) — ETA ~3m per node.

maria: while draining, let's toggle kv_cache.eviction_threshold from 0.85 -> 0.6 for the model group that spiked. That should free entries proactively. Akshay, can you push the config?

akshay: pushing now to staging then prod via rollout-cfg. Command: `rb config set model.group.kv_cache.eviction_threshold 0.6 --env prod --target serving-pool-7`

akshay: applied to canary subset. Watching metrics.

(2m) maria: OOMs on node-7a dropped by ~70% after eviction change but still seeing intermittent failures.

jamie: looks like compaction will be necessary. Current allocator doesn't coalesce adjacent small blocks due to reserved-block meta pinned by inactive tensors. We can trigger a soft restart of the runtime process to reclaim scattered free slabs as a short-term. Thoughts?

kevin: soft restart + temporarily reducing per-request max-length to 2048 tokens for the canary could reduce pressure on KV cache and prevent large allocations until we have a long-term fix.

maria: propose: 1) reduce max-length on canary -> 2048, 2) soft restart runtime on nodes drained then bring them back, 3) continue draining remaining nodes, 4) if errors persist rollback model variant. Who wants to own execution?

akshay: I can handle the config change (max-length) and kv eviction. Jamie — can you coordinate restart of runtime? Kevin — handle drain with ops-bot. I'll monitor customer-facing errors.

jamie: I'll do the soft restarts. Plan: for each node after drain, `systemctl restart redwood-runtime` and monitor memory map. We'll wait 30s between nodes.

kevin: ops-bot: continue drain on node-7c, 7d.
ops-bot: drain in progress. moving 7c now.

(5m later) akshay: max-length applied. customer 503 rate dropped from 5% -> 0.8%. KV cache size trending down (8.4k -> 4.1k entries).

jamie: started soft restarts on 7a (done), 7b (in progress). Post-restart allocator fragmentation metrics: median_free_block increased from 12MB -> 48MB, max_free_block -> 600MB on restarted nodes.

maria: good signal. but we still have a couple of requests hitting allocation >512MB and OOMing on one node that hasn't been rotated. Drain will finish in ~6m.

kevin: ops-bot: complete drain on 7c and 7d, mark node-7b as in-service after restart.
ops-bot: drains completed for 7c,7d. 7b restart completed and healthy.

maria: handing off to next oncall for postmortem and long-term fix tracking. Summary for handoff:
- Root cause (likely): allocator fragmentation + reserved block accounting mismatch with KV cache growth causing large contiguous allocation failures despite reported headroom.
- Immediate mitigations taken: kv_cache.eviction_threshold lowered, per-request max-length reduced on canary, soft restart of runtime processes to defragment free lists, drained affected nodes and shifted traffic.
- Customer impact: brief spike of 503s (~20m window) affecting long-context chat requests for ~2% of active customers on the canary model; no data loss reported.
- Next steps: schedule change to allocator to support on-the-fly coalescing of adjacent free blocks, add reservation accounting for cached KV entries, add circuit-breaker to avoid allocating >max_free_block-sized chunks and trigger fallback to smaller model variant or streaming chunking.

jamie: I'll open the incident ticket and link this thread. assigning to `eng-runtime` and `eng-ml` for allocator + KV cache follow-up.

akshay: monitoring for 30m, but from current view things are stable. leaving watch to SRE handoff.

kevin: thanks team. handing to @oncall-next for 0300-0600 slot. please pick up postmortem and P0->P1 cleanup. :thumbsup:
